evidence: Independent symbolic checks of the displayed Alexander and Jones polynomials give a2=52, a4=681, V''(1)=-312, V'''(1)=-10692, and v3=323/4 in the record's normalization.

The finite-type numerator is 7*52^2-52-10*681=12066, hence C0=12066/(8*(323/4))=6033/323 in lowest terms. Therefore a same-sign chirally cosmetic pair governed by the Ichihara-Ito-Saito slope equation requires 6033 to divide the surgery numerator m, excluding 1<=|m|<=30.

Varvarezos' L-space-knot theorem excludes opposite-sign chirally cosmetic slopes. The 0-type alternative is excluded by v3!=0 under the cited Ichihara-Ito-Saito constraint. Distinct integral slopes also have different first-homology orders.

The committed master verifier derives the same Alexander/Conway/Jones data from the frozen positive four-braid word and includes trefoil controls; no withdrawn d-invariant calculation is used by the headline proof.
Ichihara-Ito-Saito and Varvarezos provide general surgery obstructions rather than this per-knot t12533 evaluation.

Baker-Teragaito identify t12533 as the exceptional braid-index-four asymmetric L-space census knot. Targeted comparison did not locate the exact package a2=52, a4=681, v3=323/4, C0=6033/323 or the |H1|<=30 exclusion in prior literature.
Novelty is claimed only for the exact per-knot computation/application, not for the obstruction theorems.
t12533 is a literature-motivated asymmetric hyperbolic L-space census knot, so an exact chiral-surgery exclusion on a concrete homology range is a reusable datum rather than an arbitrary test case.

The computation packages several exact finite-type invariants and a divisibility obstruction that can be reused in future surgery classifications. The scope is explicitly finite and does not overstate a global no-cosmetic-surgery theorem.
